title: Common finite extension of finitely many complete traits
statement: Let $W_0$ be a complete discrete valuation ring with fraction field $K_0$ and residue field $k_0$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring, def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring, def-weil-field]. Let $I$ be a finite set. For each $i\in I$, let $W_i$ be a complete discrete valuation ring equipped with an injective local map $W_0\hookrightarrow W_i$ and finite fraction-field extension $\operatorname{Frac}(W_i)/K_0$ [def-pc-field-extension, def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Then there exists a complete discrete valuation ring $W$ with an injective local map $W_0\hookrightarrow W$ making $W$ finite as a $W_0$-module and, for every $i$, a local $W_0$-map $W_i\hookrightarrow W$. The residue field $W/\mathfrak m_W$ [def-weil-residue-field] is a finite extension of $k_0$; if $k_0$ is perfect, so is this residue field. Here a ring map between local rings is local when the inverse image of the target maximal ideal is the source maximal ideal; a perfect field has characteristic zero, or has characteristic $p>0$ with surjective Frobenius $x\mapsto x^p$.

source.place: Expose IV §4.2.3, sentence beginning De tels idéaux p étant en nombre fini: choose one finite base change dominating the finitely many Epp extensions

proof.text: Write $K_i=\operatorname{Frac}(W_i)$. Enumerate the finite set $I$ and inductively construct a finite extension $L_j/K_0$ receiving the first $j$ fields. Start with $L_0=K_0$. Given $L_j$, [lem-weil-common-extension-fields] embeds $L_j$ and the next $K_i$ over $K_0$ in one field $\Omega$. In $\Omega$ take their compositum $L_{j+1}$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-compositum-degree-bound] with $F=K_0$, $K$ the image of $K_i$, and $M$ the image of $L_j$: it gives that $L_{j+1}/L_j$ is finite. If $a_r$ span $L_j/K_0$ and $b_s$ span $L_{j+1}/L_j$, the finitely many products $a_rb_s$ span $L_{j+1}/K_0$, by expanding coefficients in the $a_r$. The old embeddings compose with the inclusion of $L_j$ in $L_{j+1}$. At the end obtain a finite extension $L/K_0$ and $K_0$-embeddings $\sigma_i:K_i\hookrightarrow L$. For $I=\varnothing$ take $L=K_0$.

source.place: Tag 0H7K (lemma-common-extension-field) and Tag 09ID (definition-compositum); finite iteration spelling out the common base extension in ILO IV 4.2.3

proof.text: Let $W\subseteq L$ be the integral closure of $W_0$ in $L$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Apply [lem-per-complete-dvr-finite-normalization] with $A=W_0$, $K=K_0$: the hypotheses are exactly completeness of $W_0$ and the finiteness of $L/K_0$ from step 1. Thus $W$ is a complete DVR, its fraction field is $L$, and $W_0\hookrightarrow W$ is injective, local and finite as a module. For each $i$, apply the uniqueness assertion of the same node to $A=W_0$, $L=K_i$ and $V=W_i$: the assumed local injection and its fraction-field extension identify $W_i$ with the integral closure of $W_0$ in $K_i$. Hence every $x\in W_i$ is integral over $W_0$. Applying $\sigma_i$ to its monic equation leaves its coefficients in $W_0$ unchanged, so $\sigma_i(x)\in W$. Restriction therefore defines an injective $W_0$-algebra map $f_i:W_i\hookrightarrow W$.

source.place: Tags 09EM (remark-construction) and 09F8 (lemma-special-case, first paragraph of proof); integral equations transported along the constructed field embeddings

proof.text: Check that each $f_i$ is local. Choose uniformizers $\pi_0\in W_0$ and $\pi_i\in W_i$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. The image of $\pi_0$ in $W_i$ is nonzero and lies in its maximal ideal, by the original injective local map. By [lem-weil-pbc-dvr-unit-times-uniformizer-power] it is $u\pi_i^e$ with $u$ a unit and $e\ge0$. In fact $e>0$, since otherwise $\pi_0$ would be a unit. In $W$ its image lies in $\mathfrak m_W$, while $f_i(u)$ remains a unit. Thus $f_i(\pi_i)^e\in\mathfrak m_W$, and primality gives $f_i(\pi_i)\in\mathfrak m_W$. Every element of $\mathfrak m_{W_i}=\pi_iW_i$ therefore maps into $\mathfrak m_W$. Every element outside $\mathfrak m_{W_i}$ is a unit and maps to a unit; this gives $f_i^{-1}(\mathfrak m_W)=\mathfrak m_{W_i}$.

source.place: Tag 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr), final uniformizer factorization assertion; elementary locality test

proof.text: Set $k=W/\mathfrak m_W$. Locality of $W_0\to W$ induces an injective field map $k_0\to k$: its kernel before quotient is $\mathfrak m_{W_0}$. If $w_1,\ldots,w_t$ generate $W$ as a $W_0$-module, their residue classes span $k$ over $k_0$, since reducing an expression $w=\sum_j a_jw_j$ gives $\bar w=\sum_j\bar a_j\bar w_j$. Thus $k/k_0$ is a finite field extension.

source.place: Expose IV 4.2.3: finite base extension W_0′/W_0; elementary residue-module calculation

proof.text: Finally suppose $k_0$ is perfect. For each $x\in k$, finite-dimensionality makes $1,x,\ldots,x^t$ linearly dependent if $t$ elements span $k$ over $k_0$, so $x$ satisfies a nonzero polynomial over $k_0$. Hence $k/k_0$ is algebraic. Apply [lem-per-algebraic-extension-perfect] to conclude that $k$ is perfect. Together with steps 2–4 this proves every assertion, including the empty-family case.

source.place: Algebra.IsAlgebraic.perfectField, lines 344–347; algebraicity of a finite-dimensional field extension checked by linear dependence
